sources: Pro Football Hall of Fame: Steelers
note: Hall of Famers who spent all or most of their careers in Pittsburgh, or are best known for their work here. No Steeler was in the Class of 2026.

players.name: Terry Bradshaw
players.text: The first overall pick in 1970 grew into the quarterback of a dynasty. He won four Super Bowls, was MVP of XIII and XIV, and was the league MVP in 1978. His deep passing made the late-’70s offense one of the NFL’s most dangerous.

players.name: Franco Harris
players.text: Made the Immaculate Reception as a rookie in 1972, the play that changed the franchise. He was MVP of Super Bowl IX and ran for 11,950 yards in Pittsburgh, still the team record. His No. 32 was retired in 2022.

players.name: Jerome Bettis
players.text: Came over from the Rams in a 1996 draft-day trade and ran for 10,571 yards in Pittsburgh. “The Bus” was nearly impossible to tackle near the goal line. He ended his career with a Super Bowl XL win in his hometown of Detroit.

players.name: John Henry Johnson
players.text: A bruising fullback who gave Pittsburgh its first 1,000-yard rushing seasons, in 1962 and 1964. He was also a punishing blocker. He went into Canton in 1987.

players.name: Bill Dudley
players.text: “Bullet Bill” did everything: run, pass, catch, return kicks and intercept passes. He led the league in rushing as a rookie in 1942. After returning from military service, he was named the league’s MVP in 1946.

players.name: Lynn Swann
players.text: A graceful receiver known for acrobatic catches in big games. He was the MVP of Super Bowl X. He won four Super Bowls.

players.name: John Stallworth
players.text: A fourth-round pick from Alabama A&M, found through Bill Nunn’s scouting. He caught long touchdowns in Super Bowls XIII and XIV. He was later a part-owner of the team.

players.name: Mike Webster
players.text: “Iron Mike” started at center on four Super Bowl champions and made nine Pro Bowls. He set the tone for the offensive line for 15 seasons. He was inducted into Canton in 1997.

players.name: Dermontti Dawson
players.text: Followed Mike Webster at center and somehow kept the standard just as high. He was fast enough to pull and lead the way on running plays, which was rare for a center. He made seven straight Pro Bowls and went into Canton in 2012.

players.name: Alan Faneca
players.text: A 1998 first-round pick who became one of the best guards in football. His pulling block helped spring Willie Parker’s 75-yard touchdown run in Super Bowl XL. He made seven Pro Bowls as a Steeler and was inducted into Canton in 2021.

players.name: Walt Kiesling
players.text: A Hall of Fame lineman who finished his playing career in Pittsburgh. He served as head coach in three different stints. He was involved with the team for most of its first three decades.

players.name: Joe Greene
players.text: Chuck Noll’s first draft pick, in 1969, and the cornerstone of the Steel Curtain. “Mean Joe” was Defensive Player of the Year twice and set the tone for four Super Bowl champions. He later coached the defensive line for Noll.

players.name: Ernie Stautner
players.text: An undersized but relentless defensive tackle who played 14 seasons in Pittsburgh. He made nine Pro Bowls. He was the face of the franchise in the 1950s.

players.name: Jack Ham
players.text: An outside linebacker so smart and smooth that he almost never seemed out of position. He finished with 32 interceptions and 21 fumble recoveries and was the 1975 Defensive Player of the Year. He won four Super Bowls.

players.name: Jack Lambert
players.text: The snarling, gap-toothed middle linebacker of the Steel Curtain. He was the 1976 Defensive Player of the Year and made nine straight Pro Bowls. He won four Super Bowls.

players.name: Kevin Greene
players.text: Spent just three seasons in Pittsburgh but made them count. The free-agent pass rusher led the NFL with 14 sacks in 1994 and helped the team reach Super Bowl XXX. His career sack total took him to Canton in 2016.

players.name: Mel Blount
players.text: A big, physical cornerback who was the 1975 Defensive Player of the Year. He was so tough on receivers that the league changed its contact rules in 1978. His 57 interceptions are still the team record, and he won four Super Bowls.

players.name: Jack Butler
players.text: An undrafted cornerback from St. Bonaventure who became one of the best ball hawks of the 1950s. He picked off 52 passes before a knee injury ended his career. He was inducted into Canton in 2012.

players.name: Rod Woodson
players.text: The 10th pick in 1987, he was a shutdown corner and a dangerous returner. He was the 1993 Defensive Player of the Year. He came back from a torn ACL to play in Super Bowl XXX and was inducted into Canton in 2009.

players.name: Donnie Shell
players.text: An undrafted safety from South Carolina State who hit like a linebacker. When he retired, he had more interceptions (51) than any other strong safety in history. He won four Super Bowls and was inducted into Canton in 2020.

players.name: Troy Polamalu
players.text: A 2003 first-round pick whose long hair and wild instincts made him one of the most famous defenders of his era. He was the 2010 Defensive Player of the Year and made eight Pro Bowls. He won two Super Bowls and was inducted into Canton in 2020.

builders.name: Art Rooney Sr.
builders.text: Founded the team in 1933 as the Pirates. “The Chief” was known for his loyalty, his cigars and his ties to the city. He saw the team go from decades of struggles to four Super Bowl titles.

builders.name: Dan Rooney
builders.text: The founder’s son, who ran the team for decades as president and then chairman. He helped hire Chuck Noll and set the team’s steady style. The Rooney Rule for minority hiring is named for him, and he later served as U.S. ambassador to Ireland.

builders.name: Chuck Noll
builders.text: Took over a losing franchise in 1969 and built a dynasty through the draft. He won four Super Bowls in six seasons, still the most in league history at the time. He coached 23 seasons and was inducted into Canton in 1993.

builders.name: Bill Cowher
builders.text: A Pittsburgh-area native who took over for Chuck Noll in 1992 at age 34. His jaw-out intensity defined the team for 15 seasons, which included 10 playoff trips and two Super Bowl appearances. He won Super Bowl XL and made the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2020.

builders.name: Bill Nunn
builders.text: A Pittsburgh Courier sportswriter who joined the scouting staff and opened doors at historically Black colleges. He helped find players like John Stallworth, Donnie Shell and L.C. Greenwood. He was inducted into Canton in 2021.

brief.name: Cal Hubbard
brief.text: A towering lineman who starred for the Giants and Packers and spent one season with the 1936 Pirates. He is also in baseball’s Hall of Fame as an umpire.

brief.name: Johnny “Blood” McNally
brief.text: Best known for his Packers years, he played for and coached the Pirates in the late 1930s. A charter member of the Hall.

brief.name: Bert Bell
brief.text: Co-owned the team with Art Rooney in the early 1940s and briefly coached it. He became NFL commissioner and created the college draft.

brief.name: Bobby Layne
brief.text: Earned his bust with the Lions, then finished with five seasons in Pittsburgh after a 1958 trade.

brief.name: Marion Motley
brief.text: The Browns’ great fullback and pass protector finished his career with a short stint in Pittsburgh in 1955.

brief.name: Johnny Unitas
brief.text: A Pittsburgh native the Steelers drafted in 1955 and cut in training camp before he ever played a regular-season game. He became a legend with the Colts.

brief.name: Len Dawson
brief.text: A first-round pick who barely played in three Pittsburgh seasons. He became a champion with the Chiefs.

brief.name: Jim Finks
brief.text: Played quarterback and defensive back in Pittsburgh. He made the Hall as a team builder for the Vikings, Bears and Saints.

brief.name: Mike Munchak
brief.text: A Hall of Fame guard with the Oilers who later coached the Steelers’ offensive line.

brief.name: Russ Grimm
brief.text: A Washington “Hog” in his playing days, he coached the line for the Super Bowl XL team.

brief.name: Dick LeBeau
brief.text: Inducted for his Lions playing career, but Steelers fans know him for the zone blitz defenses that won two Super Bowls.

brief.name: Tony Dungy
brief.text: Played safety on the Super Bowl XIII team and later coached Pittsburgh’s secondary and defense. He went into the Hall as a head coach with the Colts.
